doc.title: Milt Hinton interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

title: Teaching young musicians in schools in place of band apprenticeships
summary: Hinton says young players lack the apprenticeship he had under Calloway, and that teaching in schools with Clark Terry must replace it.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Well I feel sorry, and that’s the reason I think so wonderful of you, and I see you out working and that’s what I do a great deal of, is trying to go around to the schools now, and impart some knowledge to these young people because they don’t have an

apprenticeship, for them to come in like we came in, like I came in Cab Calloway’s band with all these giants, Ben Webster, and Cab, and Doc Cheatham, you know, and I got a chance to learn something about discipline and things like that. We don’t have those bands for our young musicians, as with the masters, to sit down and watch them.
So we have to try to do that in the schools.
We’re trying to do that, and I know you are, and Clark Terry is a masterful at that kind of thing.
I learned so much from him doing that, and so —
